/-!
# Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture

The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture on $\chi$-boundedness of graphs with a forbidden induced tree.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C3%A1rf%C3%A1s%E2%80%93Sumner_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gy75] A. Gyárfás, *On Ramsey covering-numbers*, Infinite and finite sets (Colloq., Keszthely,
  1973), Vol. II, North-Holland, 1975.
- [Su81] D. P. Sumner, *Subtrees of a graph and the chromatic number*, The theory and applications
  of graphs (Kalamazoo, Mich., 1980), Wiley, 1981.
-/

blocks.docstring:
**Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.** For any fixed pair of a tree $T$ and a complete graph $K_t$, the
graphs that are both $T$-free and $K_t$-free are $\chi$-bounded. That is, for every finite tree
$T$ and every $t$, there is a constant $c$ (depending only on $T$ and $t$) such that every finite
graph $G$ containing neither $T$ nor $K_t$ as an induced subgraph satisfies $\chi(G) \le c$.

Here `T ⊴ G` means that `G` has an induced subgraph isomorphic to `T` (there is a graph embedding
`T ↪g G`), and `G.CliqueFree t` means that `G` has no clique on `t` vertices, i.e. no induced
subgraph isomorphic to $K_t$. A tree is a connected acyclic graph, so `T` is nonempty.

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop: for every finite tree T (connected, acyclic, hence nonempty) and every t, there is a constant c (depending only on T and t) such that every finite simple graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to T and no clique of size t has chromatic number at most c; quantifier order is ∀ T, ∀ t, ∃ c, ∀ G (equivalently ∀ T, ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ T-free G, χ(G) ≤ f(ω(G))), 'free' means induced-subgraph-free (not subgraph-free), and the article's 'Equivalently, every K_t-free graph of large enough χ contains T induced' is the contrapositive of the same Prop, not a separate question; the known special cases (paths, stars, radius-two trees) and the subdivision result are background theorems the list entry does not pose.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: ∀ finite tree T (SimpleGraph α, [Fintype/Finite α], T.IsTree — connected hence nonempty), ∀ t : ℕ, ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ finite G, ¬ (T inducedly contained in G) → G.CliqueFree t → G.chromaticNumber ≤ c. Verified against Mathlib source: IsIndContained T G := Nonempty (T ↪g G) (induced, not SimpleGraph.Free), chromaticNumber ≤ ↑c ↔ Colorable c, CliqueFree 0 unsatisfiable (vacuous, matching K₀ ⊆ every graph), CliqueFree 1 ↔ empty G. Quantifier order ∀T ∀t ∃c ∀G is exactly χ-boundedness with c depending only on T and t. Restricting G to finite graphs matches the standard statement (and is equivalent by de Bruijn–Erdős). c02 chosen for the theorem-argument style, Mathlib's official `⊴` notation under `open SimpleGraph`, and the most informative docstring/references; c01/c03–c08 are stylistic variants (Fintype vs Finite, Type* vs Type, ¬T.IsIndContained G / IsEmpty (T ↪g G)) of the same statement and would be equally acceptable.

context:
In graph theory, the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture says that for any fixed pair of a tree $T$ and a complete graph $K_{t}$, every graph that is both $T$ -free and $K_{t}$ -free is also $\chi$ -bounded; that is, every graph that contains neither $T$ nor $K_{t}$ as an induced subgraph can be properly colored using a constant number of colors.
Equivalently, it says that every $K_{t}$ -free graph $G$ contains any arbitrarily chosen tree $T$ (as an induced subgraph), as long as $\chi (G)$ is large enough.
It is named after András Gyárfás and David Sumner, who formulated it independently in 1975 and 1981 respectively. It remains unproven.
In this conjecture, it is not possible to replace $T$ by a graph with cycles. As Paul Erdős and András Hajnal have shown, there exist graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number and, at the same time, arbitrarily large girth. Using these graphs, one can obtain graphs that avoid any fixed choice of a cyclic graph and clique (of more than two vertices) as induced subgraphs, and exceed any fixed bound on the chromatic number.
The conjecture is known to be true for certain special choices of $T$, including paths, stars, and trees of radius two.

/-!
# Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture

The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture on $\chi$-boundedness of graphs with a forbidden induced tree.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C3%A1rf%C3%A1s%E2%80%93Sumner_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gy75] A. Gyárfás, *On Ramsey covering-numbers*, Infinite and finite sets (Colloq., Keszthely,
  1973), Vol. II, North-Holland, 1975.

namespace GyarfasSumnerConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
**Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.** For any fixed pair of a tree $T$ and a complete graph $K_t$, the
graphs that are both $T$-free and $K_t$-free are $\chi$-bounded. That is, for every finite tree
$T$ and every $t$, there is a constant $c$ (depending only on $T$ and $t$) such that every finite
graph $G$ containing neither $T$ nor $K_t$ as an induced subgraph satisfies $\chi(G) \le c$.

Here `T ⊴ G` means that `G` has an induced subgraph isomorphic to `T` (there is a graph embedding
`T ↪g G`), and `G.CliqueFree t` means that `G` has no clique on `t` vertices, i.e. no induced
subgraph isomorphic to $K_t$. A tree is a connected acyclic graph, so `T` is nonempty.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem gyarfas_sumner_conjecture {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (T : SimpleGraph α) (hT : T.IsTree)
    (t : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ {β : Type*} [Fintype β] (G : SimpleGraph β),
      ¬ T ⊴ G → G.CliqueFree t → G.chromaticNumber ≤ c := by
  sorry

end GyarfasSumnerConjecture

items: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the article's lead: ∀ tree T, ∀ t, ∃ c, ∀ G (T-free and K_t-free ⇒ χ(G) ≤ c). This quantifier order (c depends only on T and t, not on G) is what χ-boundedness of the class means.

'T-free' is modelled as induced-subgraph-free: `¬ T ⊴ G` where `SimpleGraph.IsIndContained T G := Nonempty (T ↪g G)`; a graph embedding is exactly an isomorphism onto an induced subgraph. Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Free` (non-induced copies) was deliberately NOT used.

'K_t-free' is modelled as `G.CliqueFree t`; for complete graphs, induced and non-induced containment coincide (Mathlib: `not_cliqueFree_iff : ¬G.CliqueFree n ↔ Nonempty (completeGraph (Fin n) ↪g G)`). Degenerate t: t = 0 makes the hypothesis impossible (vacuous), t = 1 forces G empty; neither changes the mathematical content.

Trees are `SimpleGraph.IsTree` (connected and acyclic); connectedness in Mathlib includes nonemptiness, so T is nonempty and `¬ T ⊴ G` is a genuine constraint (an empty T would be inducedly contained in everything). T is required finite via `[Fintype α]`, as in the standard statement.

G is restricted to finite graphs (`[Fintype β]`), following the standard finite-graph reading (and the decomposition notes). By de Bruijn–Erdős compactness the infinite-graph version is equivalent, so nothing is lost.
The chromatic number is Mathlib's `chromaticNumber : ℕ∞`; the bound is `G.chromaticNumber ≤ (c : ℕ∞)` with c : ℕ. For a finite graph χ is finite, so this is the intended inequality.
Vertex types are universe-polymorphic (`Type*`) for both T and G; since the graphs are finite this is immaterial up to isomorphism but avoids an artificial restriction to `Type`.

Only the single slot is stated. The article's 'equivalently, every K_t-free G with χ large enough contains T induced' is the contrapositive of the same proposition and is not stated separately, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: The list entry is a bare title; the precise statement was taken from the linked article's lead sentence, as the decomposition table prescribes. No candidate omitted the slot and no candidate objected to the decomposition; I agree the article's 'Equivalently ... χ large enough contains T' sentence is the contrapositive of the same Prop and the special cases (paths, stars, radius-two trees, subdivisions) are background theorems. Modeling notes: 'T-free'/'K_t-free' are induced-subgraph-free (Mathlib IsIndContained / CliqueFree, the latter coinciding with induced K_t-freeness since K_t is complete); host graphs are finite, which is the standard setting and equivalent to the infinite version by compactness; degenerate t = 0 (vacuous) and t = 1 (G empty) and one-vertex trees are handled with their literal meanings and do not distort the claim. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
